items.cold_note: Exp 1 (all K, 20.0 cm2): 75g->3.0, 150g->6.0, 225g->9.0 cm; depth = 0.04 cm/g x mass, linear through all three rows. 300 g -> 12.0 cm > 10.0 cm height, so it cannot float upright. A (10.0) and B (9.0) misextrapolate; C contradicts the table (all areas 20.0).
items.fact_error: Shared passage (Exp. 1 / Exp. 2 text): 'Four cylinders of a solid, unnamed plastic ... each with a cross-sectional area of 20.0 cm2 but with different masses', and Exp. 2 calls it 'the same solid plastic'. Every cylinder is 10.0 cm tall, so all have volume 200 cm3; one solid, non-absorbing material at fixed volume has one mass (density fixed). 75, 150, 225, 300 g of the same solid plastic at identical dimensions is physically impossible (implied densities 0.375, 0.75, 1.125, 1.5 g/cm3). The flotation numbers are otherwise internally consistent (Liquid K = 1.25 g/cm3 from every Exp. 1 row; 300 g at 1.5 g/cm3 sinks), but the setup breaks conservation of density for one material. Passage-level: it affects the whole sc9a-p5 stimulus.

free_elimination.how: Stem says the cylinder SANK. B says the needed depth is LESS than its height, which would let it float, so it contradicts the stem. C is self-contradictory physics (a larger area displaces more liquid at a given depth, not less). A is weak too ('equals its height exactly' is a borderline, not a reason to sink). Only D gives a reason to sink.
